clue.text: Series on Sky Atlantic?

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece sitting on another comes after it, so the series follows the sky

blocks.note: the sky is the air above us
a series or row of things is a line

explanation.surface: A TV schedule question: which show is airing on the Sky Atlantic channel?
explanation.walkthrough: Sky Atlantic is a British pay-TV channel, so the clue reads like a listings query. The question mark warns that 'Atlantic' defines by example: Virgin Atlantic is a carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin Atlantic is a well-known passenger carrier, so the bare name stands as an example of a flying company.

clue.text: Recognises mushroom seen in book

indicators.note: something seen in another thing sits inside it, so the fungus goes within the book

blocks.note: Acts of the Apostles, a book of the New Testament
the cep is an edible wild mushroom (porcini)

explanation.surface: Someone identifies a mushroom pictured in a field guide.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something is to acknowledge or recognise it as valid.

clue.text: Steps to put an end to drought?

definitions.text: Steps to put an end to drought?

blocks.clueFragment: Steps to put an end to drought?
blocks.note: surface reading: practical measures, like hosepipe bans or reservoirs, to end a dry spell
setter's reading: steps are dance moves, performed ritually to summon a downpour

explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' looks like policy measures; it means footwork, the ritual performed to bring on wet weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritual dance performed in some cultures to call down precipitation and end a dry spell.

clue.text: Close to tears after I bash religion

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so only the end of tears is kept
one piece placed after another follows it in the answer, so the pronoun comes first

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of tears
to lam is to thrash or beat

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a faith and is brought nearly to tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the monotheistic faith of Muslims, so it is a religion.

clue.text: Vehicle set off, about to enter a race

indicators.note: a set that is off has gone wrong, so its letters are disturbed
the abbreviation for about goes inside the word for race

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written
to tear is to race along
C stands for circa, about

explanation.surface: A car sets off just as a race is about to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' looks like the car departing, but off only signals rearranging set, and race is the verb meaning hurry. An estate car is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate car is a motor vehicle with a long rear load space, the British term for a station wagon.

clue.text: Live well in Berlin, acquiring flipping concerning drinking problem

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the short word for concerning is read the other way
the first two pieces acquire the third, taking it inside them

blocks.note: to be is to live or exist
re means concerning or about
gut is German for well or good

explanation.surface: Someone lives the good life in Berlin, worrying about a drinking habit along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well in Berlin' asks for the German word. A beer gut is a belly swollen by heavy beer drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A paunch caused by too much beer is a physical problem that comes from drinking, so the phrase is fair.

clue.text: British nurse caught leaving wearing less

indicators.note: when the abbreviation for caught is leaving, it departs from the word for nurse

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a carer looks after the sick, as a nurse does
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A British nurse is caught leaving work in scanty clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Barer is the comparative of bare, so it describes someone less covered or clothed.

clue.text: The blaze spreads, engulfing India's former head of state

indicators.note: a fire that spreads moves its parts around, so these letters scatter
the flames engulf the letter for India, closing round it

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A fire spreads and swallows up the place where India's ex-president lived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'India's former head of state' reads as one phrase; India only supplies a letter, and the definition is the late British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Elizabeth II was the British sovereign and head of state until her death in 2022.

clue.text: Police pull up outside university

indicators.note: in a down answer going up means the word is read from the bottom
the turned word goes outside the abbreviation, wrapping it

blocks.note: to drag is to pull
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Police raid a university, pulling up outside the campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police' looks like a noun for officers, but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To police an area is to watch over and protect it, which is what it means to guard it.

clue.text: Whistle-blower infiltrates industry plant

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so the official goes into the word for industry

blocks.note: industry as hard work, toil
a referee blows the whistle in a match

explanation.surface: An informant gets inside an industrial plant to expose wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistle-blower' suggests an informant and 'plant' a factory; they are a referee and a growing thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Trefoil is a clover-like herb with three-part leaves, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Check I'm going to relax

blocks.note: CH is chess notation for check
I'll, short for I will, says I'm going to

explanation.surface: Someone checks their schedule and decides to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: To chill, or chill out, is slang for unwinding and taking it easy.

clue.text: Stop and start on time after golf shot

indicators.note: in an across answer a word placed on another comes after it, so the time abbreviation leads
to be shot of something is to be rid of it, so the golf letter is thrown away

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a seed starts to grow when it germinates
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfer is told to finish up and tee off promptly after a stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golf shot' reads as one stroke on the course; it is golf's letter being got rid of. 'Start' is a seed sprouting.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate something is to bring it to an end, to stop it.

clue.text: Sports nut getting fitter, wanting suitable exercise tracker

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word for suitable is missing from the bigger word

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school sports
nut and dome are both slang for the head
taken as written
fit means suitable or appropriate

explanation.surface: A sports fanatic gets into shape but is missing the right gadget to log workouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sports nut' reads as a fan, but sports and nut are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedometer counts steps walked, so it is a device for tracking physical activity.

clue.text: Recording of old princess wearing gold ring

indicators.note: something worn goes around its wearer, so the metal surrounds the princess

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
Di was the familiar name of Diana, the late Princess of Wales
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A recording of the late Princess of Wales wearing a gold ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio is sound, as in an audio recording, so a recording of sound alone can be called audio.

clue.text: Nitrogen-fuelled rocket's navigation aid

indicators.note: fuel goes inside an engine, so the chemical symbol is put inside the word for rocket

blocks.note: to rocket is to soar, climb steeply
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A rocket fuelled by nitrogen carries its own navigation equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocket' looks like a noun for a missile; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonar locates objects underwater by sound echoes, which ships and submarines use to navigate.

clue.text: Does cur get briefly abandoned, becoming this?

definitions.text: Does cur get briefly abandoned, becoming this?

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of get is dropped
abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: Is a dog that gets abandoned destined to end up in a shelter?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a mongrel that gets abandoned may become one taken in by a shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescue dog is one rehomed from a shelter after being abandoned, so an abandoned cur becomes one.

clue.text: Start to chew the fat, going back to take in a grand building

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of chew is kept
going back means the word for fat is read in the opposite direction
the assembled letters take in the article, holding it inside them

blocks.note: the first letter of chew
taken as written
lard is pig fat
taken as written

explanation.surface: People start chatting idly as they head back into a grand building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chew the fat' is an idiom for chatting, which hides that chew, the and fat each do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is a large principal church, the seat of a bishop, so it is a grand building.

clue.text: Take a risk – support keeping president and prime minister around

indicators.note: turned around means the pair of names is read the other way
the support keeps the other letters inside it

blocks.note: a golf tee supports the ball
William Howard Taft was the 27th US president
PM is the abbreviation for prime minister

explanation.surface: A political gamble: backing a coalition of president and prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The president is a US one, William Howard Taft.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt fate is to act in a way that invites misfortune, which is to take a risk.

clue.text: Undoing general's reforms before one's introduced

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters are rearranged
something introduced is put in, so the numeral goes inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged, the apostrophe ignored
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A general's reforms are being reversed before someone new is brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: Releasing a knot or fastening means undoing it, setting it free.

clue.text: Master grabs student before mass, causing turmoil

indicators.note: to grab is to hold within one's grasp, so the master encloses the learner
before places the enclosed group ahead of the mass letter

blocks.note: a maestro is a master of an art, especially music
L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate
m is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster seizes a pupil just before church, causing chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a violent whirlpool, and figuratively a scene of confused turmoil.

clue.text: Suggest doctor takes drug for wind

indicators.note: the doctor takes the drug in, holding it inside

blocks.note: to mean is to suggest or imply
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone advises that a doctor prescribe medicine for flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' suggests flatulence beside the doctor and drug; it is the verb rhyming with find, as a river winds.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to follow a winding, twisting course, as a river does.

clue.text: Welcome love ending misery

indicators.note: a piece ending another is placed at its end, so the letter for love comes last

blocks.note: hell is utter misery
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A warm welcome from a lover brings someone's unhappiness to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is the greeting used to welcome someone on meeting them.

clue.text: Bobby regularly stays in parts of Ukraine, Belarus etc

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the name is kept

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of Bobby
to last is to stay or endure

explanation.surface: A policeman routinely stays in various regions of eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is a British police officer, but here the name only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblast is an administrative region or province in Ukraine, Belarus and Russia.

clue.text: See you in uniform, following war reporter

indicators.note: the uniform letter follows, coming after the reporter's name

blocks.note: Kate Adie is a famous BBC war correspondent
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A farewell to someone in military uniform, after a war correspondent's report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See you in uniform' looks like one phrase; the definition ends at you. Kate Adie reported from many wars for the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French for goodbye, a parting phrase like see you.

clue.text: A little princeling, one who thinks he deserves it?

definitions.text: one who thinks he deserves it?

indicators.note: a little of the word means only a part of it, a run of its letters

blocks.note: the run of letters inside this word

explanation.surface: A minor prince who believes he is owed something.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'it' can mean sex. An incel, involuntary celibate, is a man who resents being denied sex and feels entitled to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Incels typically feel entitled to sex and blame others for not getting it, so the question-marked phrase describes one.

clue.text: Alert distributed to hen party

indicators.note: distributed means handed out in different places, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a ball is a formal dancing party

explanation.surface: An alert is sent round to everyone going on a hen party.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is a British bride's pre-wedding night out, but here 'hen party' splits into fodder and a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the ball is quick-witted and attentive, an idiom for alert.

clue.text: Illusions of perception and related trickery, primarily

definitions.text: Illusions of perception and related trickery, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: the initial letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A description of visual illusions and the tricks that go with them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer while its words' first letters spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is 1960s abstract art using patterns that create optical illusions of movement and depth.

clue.text: Pop icon trapped by hotel visitor

indicators.note: something trapped by words is held within them, so the answer sits inside the phrase

blocks.note: the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: A famous pop star gets stuck in a hotel by a guest.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the King's song Heartbreak Hotel makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley, the King of Rock and Roll, is one of the most famous figures in popular music.

clue.text: Programme made by our dad almost came out

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of came is dropped
out can mean disordered or not in place, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: A TV show about how our father came out as gay.
explanation.definitionFit: A docudrama is a TV programme or film dramatising real events.

clue.text: Very old ex-Tory leader cancels

blocks.note: v is the abbreviation for very
O is the abbreviation for old
IDS is Iain Duncan Smith, Conservative Party leader 2001 to 2003

explanation.surface: An elderly former Conservative leader calls things off.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tories are Britain's Conservative Party; their ex-leader is known by his initials.
explanation.definitionFit: To void a contract or ticket is to cancel it, declaring it of no legal effect.

clue.text: Fire again, just over the French in retreat

indicators.note: something in retreat goes backwards, so the French article is read in reverse
the word for just goes over, covering the turned article on both sides

blocks.note: just and right both mean fair
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French troops in retreat, with a soldier ordered to open fire again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like a soldier's order to shoot; it means set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: To relight a fire, candle or pilot light is to ignite it again.

clue.text: European houses adopting new standards

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the letter for new is taken into the other letters

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
N is the abbreviation for new
the twelve houses of the zodiac are the star signs

explanation.surface: European homes are taking on new building regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standards' looks like regulations; it means flags.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag or banner, and ensigns are flags, especially naval ones.
